**Imjin War (1592–1598)** – also known as the Japanese invasions of Korea – was a major conflict between the Japanese forces led by Toyotomi Hideyoshi and the Korean Joseon dynasty, with support from Ming China. Here’s a concise overview: | Aspect | Details | |--------|---------| | **Timeline** | 1592–1598 | | **Key Players** | • **Japan** – Toyotomi Hideyoshi’s forces (≈300,000 troops).
• **Korea (Joseon)** – King Seonjo, military leaders such as Admiral Yi Sun-sin.
• **Ming China** – Chinese Ming dynasty troops and naval support. | | **Causes** | • Hideyoshi’s ambition to conquer China via Korea.
• Korean refusal to allow Japanese troops to use Korean territory as a staging ground. | | **Major Phases** | 1. **First Invasion (1592–1593)** – Japanese forces quickly captured Seoul and much of the peninsula.
2. **Second Invasion (1597–1598)** – After a brief truce, Japan returned with a larger army; the war ended with the withdrawal of Japanese forces. | | **Key Battles** | • **Battle of Hansan Island** – Admiral Yi Sun-sin’s naval victory using turtle ships.
• **Siege of Jinju** – Korean defenders held out against Japanese siege.
• **Battle of Noryang** – Final naval engagement where Yi Sun-sin died. | | **Outcome** | • Japan withdrew after Hideyoshi’s death and internal strife.
• Korea suffered massive destruction and loss of life (estimates 200,000–400,000 casualties).
• Strengthened Korean naval capabilities and national identity. | | **Historical Significance** | • Demonstrated the effectiveness of naval power and innovative ship design (turtle ships).
